title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing?
abstract: arXiv:2610.19767v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI-text detection generally asks whether a machine wrote a text. As AI becomes an increasingly integral and accepted part of writing, the more relevant question is no longer whether AI was used, but how much of the text reflects human contribution. A prominent line of work estimates this by measuring how predictive a person's prompt is of the final text. We show that this measure can be easily manipulated. We introduce SPECIFICITY PADDING that simply asks the model to copy a few random IDs from the prompt, and that alone makes a title-only request look more human than one that supplies the article's key ideas. A context-swap audit then holds each document fixed, and only shows or hides the IDs to the evaluator. The score of the unchanged text swings by a third to half of its scale, and it rises for every document we test, on news and scientific abstracts, across varied LLMs from 3.8B to 753B parameters. The same articles can average 85\%

translated_title: 似然并非作者身份：我们能可靠地衡量AI辅助写作中的人类贡献吗？
translated_abstract: AI文本检测通常关注的是某段文本是否由机器撰写。随着AI日益成为写作中不可或缺且被广泛接受的一部分，更相关的问题不再是是否使用了AI，而是文本中有多少反映了人类的贡献。一项主流研究方法通过测量人的提示词对最终文本的预测能力来估计这一贡献。我们证明这种度量方式很容易被操纵。我们提出了“特异性填充”（SPECIFICITY PADDING）方法，只需让模型复制提示词中的几个随机ID，仅此一项就能让仅提供标题的请求看起来比提供了文章核心思想的请求更具“人类感”。随后的上下文交换审计保持每份文档完全不变，仅向评估器显示或隐藏这些ID。未做任何修改的文本评分会在其量级的三分之一到一半之间波动，并且在所有测试文档上都会上升，涵盖新闻和科学摘要，跨越从3.8B到753B参数的多种大语言模型。相同的文章平均可以达到85%（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文揭示了基于提示词预测能力来衡量AI辅助写作中人类贡献的方法极易被操纵——仅需让模型复制几个随机ID的“特异性填充”技巧，就能使未改变文本的评分波动达量级的三分之一到一半，证明似然并非衡量作者身份的可靠指标。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that likelihood-based measures of human contribution in AI-assisted writing are easily manipulated—simply prompting the model to copy a few random IDs ("specificity padding") swings scores of unchanged texts by a third to half of their scale across various LLMs, showing that likelihood is not a reliable proxy for authorship.
